title: Feed every ruling back to the checker
statement: When a flagged item is ruled fine, record the ruling where the checker reads it, so the same false flag doesn't come back on later runs.
detail: The content audit for Grade 3 reading lessons decides which unfamiliar words to flag from a grade-3 known-word list. Each time a lesson is adjudicated, a word found to be known is added there, which silences its false flags on every later run, and the audit's notes call the list accumulated judgment, not a static config (`shadow/content-eval/README.md`).
against: The list lags the rulings: "The other high-priority unexplained-word candidates are known at grade 3; I haven't added them to `grade3_known_words.txt`." (`shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L2-review.md`, line 94).

evidence.quote: `references/grade3_known_words.txt` is the grade-3 baseline that decides which unfamiliar words are worth flagging.
It improves every time a lesson is adjudicated — adding a genuinely-known word there silences its false flags across all future runs. Treat it as accumulated judgment, not a static config.

So a `grade-5.json` run is expected to report **4 findings**, all noise. Treat a 5th as new and adjudicate it. Do not add a suppression list — the whole file is four lines of prose and re-reading it is cheaper than maintaining exact-string exemptions that rot the moment a lesson is edited.

A `grade-5.json` run is currently EXPECTED to report 4 claim-fidelity, 1 key-integrity and 10 forward-reference findings, all adjudicated or documented as noise. Treat anything beyond those counts as new.
The rule for adding here: a limit is recorded only after the finding has been checked against the passage and judged, with the evidence written down.
It is an exact-string list of content that predates a rule.
Spot-checked, not adjudicated one by one, so the count is a baseline to beat rather than a ruling
This worked: zero re-litigated rulings across three agents. An unbriefed agent burns its round re-flagging what a ruling already closed.
An unbriefed reviewer re-discovers our own settled decisions and drowns the real gaps.
